title: The Pluperfect and Future Perfect
subtitle: ἐλελύκη, λελύσομαι — rare but worth knowing.
objectives: Form and conjugate the pluperfect active and middle/passive.
Form and conjugate the future perfect active and middle/passive.
Understand the pluperfect as expressing a past state.
Understand the future perfect as expressing a future state.

sections.heading: The pluperfect and future perfect
sections.body:
The pluperfect expresses a state that existed in the past. ἐλελύκη means 'I had loosed' or 'I was in the state of having loosed'. The future perfect expresses a state that will exist in the future. λελύσομαι means 'I will have loosed' or 'I will be in the state of having loosed'.

Both tenses are rare in Greek. The pluperfect appears in narrative; the future perfect is almost never used. But you should recognize them when you see them.

sections.heading: The pluperfect active: ἐλελύκη
sections.body:
singular
  1st   ἐλελύκη     I had loosed
  2nd   ἐλελύκης    you had loosed
  3rd   ἐλελύκει    he/she/it had loosed

  plural
  1st   ἐλελύκεμεν  we had loosed
  2nd   ἐλελύκετε   you (plural) had loosed
  3rd   ἐλελύκεσαν  they had loosed

The pluperfect uses the augment ἐ- + reduplication + perfect stem + secondary endings. The endings look like the imperfect.

sections.heading: The future perfect active: λελύσομαι
sections.body:
The future perfect is formed with the perfect stem + future endings. It is rare and usually middle/passive in form even when active in meaning.

  λελύσομαι   I will have loosed

The future perfect is so rare that you can treat it as a curiosity. If you see it, recognize that it means 'will have X-ed'.

items.answer: A state that existed in the past — 'had X-ed'.

items.prompt: What does the future perfect express?
items.answer: A state that will exist in the future — 'will have X-ed'.

items.prompt: How common is the future perfect?
